screening.reason: Applies a novel empirical-Bayes connectivity normalization method to ABIDE (UCLA site) resting-state fMRI data in an ASD-vs-TC group-difference analysis, satisfying inclusion 2-3; not purely a methods paper since it performs and reports an autism-vs-control connectivity comparison.

evidence_spans.text: This data set was collected at Brain Mapping Center in University of California, Los Angles (UCLA), one of the data collecting sites in the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE)
evidence_spans.claim: Data example is the UCLA site of ABIDE.

evidence_spans.text: initially 33 participants (typical controls, TC) and 49 patients with the Autism spectrum disorders (ASD) were asked to lie as still as possible
evidence_spans.claim: Initial sample was 33 TC and 49 ASD before motion exclusion.

evidence_spans.text: Participants with large motions were removed from the dataset, resulting in 32 participants in the TC group and 41 in the ASD group.
evidence_spans.claim: After motion-based exclusion, final sample was 32 TC and 41 ASD.

evidence_spans.text: We then use the ﬁrst 90 AAL ROIs as nodes, and take the average of all voxels’ temporal proﬁles within each ROI as region level signal for all subjects
evidence_spans.claim: Used the first 90 AAL ROIs as connectivity nodes.

evidence_spans.text: the analysis based on empirical Bayes normalized connectivity metrics shows signiﬁcant connectivity diﬀerences between the ASD and TC groups , and 44 connectivity features have fdr q- values less than 0.1.
evidence_spans.claim: After empirical-Bayes normalization, 44 connectivity features differed significantly between ASD and TC (fdr q<0.1), whereas raw correlations found none.

evidence_spans.text: No signiﬁcant feature or network is identiﬁed after the correction for the original correlations (q-value 0.1 as threshold for local fdr and permutation p-value 0.05 for NBS).
evidence_spans.claim: Raw (non-normalized) connectivity metrics found no significant group differences with the same correction thresholds.

evidence_spans.text: The ASD group show higher function connectivity between pairs of ROIs for all
evidence_spans.claim: The 44 significant features showed higher (hyper-) connectivity in ASD relative to TC.

evidence_spans.text: These results suggest that hyper-connectivity in ASD spans multiple functional subsystems of the human brain.
evidence_spans.claim: Main interpretive finding: hyper-connectivity in ASD across multiple functional subsystems.

assessments.support: Diagnostic inclusion criteria for ASD/TC groups are not detailed beyond citing the ABIDE/UCLA site source.
Single site (UCLA), scanner and acquisition parameters, and N before/after motion exclusion given.
Slice-time/motion correction, MNI registration, bandpass filter and smoothing described, but no named pipeline/software or version given.
ASD/TC diagnosis labels are taken from the ABIDE/UCLA data without the diagnostic instrument being restated in this paper.
Motion-based exclusion applied ('large motions' removed) but no quantitative FD threshold; age/sex are not reported as covariates in the sections read.
Only a qualitative motion-exclusion criterion is given; no explicit covariate adjustment for age/sex/site (single site, so no site covariate needed).
Standard Pearson correlation among 90 AAL ROIs, Fisher z-transformed, is a conventional connectivity metric; the paper's own contribution is a normalization layer on top of it.
Both local fdr (q=0.1) and Network Based Statistics (permutation p=0.05) multiple-comparison corrections applied and compared between normalized and raw metrics.

risk_of_bias.summary: A methods-focused paper whose real-data illustration is a single-site (UCLA) ABIDE analysis with adequate multiple-comparison correction but under-specified diagnostic/motion-threshold detail, since the primary contribution is the normalization method rather than the clinical finding.

charting.title: An empirical Bayes normalization method for connectivity metrics in resting state fMRI
charting.new_dataset_contributed: no — contributes a normalization method, applied to public ABIDE (UCLA) data
charting.dataset_openly_available: Uses the publicly shared ABIDE data; no new dataset or code repository link found in text
charting.specific_features: Pearson correlation (Fisher z-transformed) among the first 90 AAL ROIs, re-expressed via a novel empirical-Bayes local-fdr normalization function g(z)
charting.feature_extraction_tools: AAL atlas (first 90 ROIs); custom empirical-Bayes normalization (R package locfdr)
charting.feature_change_direction: Higher (hyper-)connectivity in ASD vs TC for 44 ROI-pair features detected only after empirical-Bayes normalization (not detectable with raw correlations)
charting.summary_key_findings: An empirical-Bayes normalization of pairwise AAL-ROI connectivity metrics revealed 44 significantly different (fdr q<0.1) connectivity features between ASD (n=41) and TC (n=32) in a single ABIDE (UCLA) site, all showing hyper-connectivity in ASD across distant functional subsystems; the same analysis on raw (non-normalized) correlations found no significant features with equivalent correction.
charting.features_associated_disorder: Hyper-connectivity between distant ROI pairs across multiple functional subsystems in ASD
charting.reviewer_notes: Primarily a statistical-methods paper; the ABIDE analysis is a real-data illustration of the method, not the paper's main contribution.

narrative_row.study_design_sample_dataset: Group-difference (associational), methods-illustration; ABIDE I, UCLA site only; n=41 ASD / 32 TC after motion exclusion.
narrative_row.methods: Standard rs-fMRI preprocessing (slice-timing, motion correction, MNI registration, bandpass, smoothing); Pearson connectivity among first 90 AAL ROIs; novel empirical-Bayes local-fdr normalization applied before group comparison with fdr and NBS correction.
narrative_row.outcomes: 44 connectivity features differed significantly (fdr q<0.1) between ASD and TC after normalization (none with raw correlations), all showing ASD hyper-connectivity across distant functional subsystems.
narrative_row.key_limitations: Single site; diagnostic criteria and motion threshold not quantitatively specified; paper's primary contribution is the statistical method, with the ABIDE analysis as one illustrative example.
narrative_row.relevance_notes: Illustrates how a connectivity-normalization method changes group-difference detection on a single-site ABIDE I subset; relevant for methodological/processing comparisons in the knowledge graph rather than as a standalone clinical finding.
